case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh and Others v Lalit Kumar Verma
petitioner: State of Madhya Pradesh and Others
respondent:
Lalit Kumar Verma
Supreme Court of India

24 November 2006
Appeal (Civil) 5185 of 2006
The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1.  Respondent herein was appointed on daily wages. Indisputably, his recruitment was not made in terms of the statutory rules. No offer of appointment was also issued. He filed an application before the Labour Court purported to be for his classification in permanent category of workman. facts: Respondent was appointed on daily wages.
His recruitment was not made in terms of statutory rules.
No offer of appointment was issued.
He filed an application before the Labour Court for his classification in permanent category of workman.

An Award was made that he acquired a right for classification in the category of permanent clerk and his services could not have been terminated without complying with the provisions of Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
He was directed to be classified on the permanent basis as clerk from two years prior to the date of his filing the application, i.e., 11th November, 1991.
He was also held to be entitled to prescribed wages and thus, the amount of difference in wages of the said post and other benefits was directed to be paid.
A writ petition was preferred thereagainst by the appellants before the High Court, which was also dismissed by a learned Single Judge, opining that no case had been made out to interfere therewith.
issues: Whether the respondent was entitled to classification as a permanent employee under the provisions of Madhya Pradesh Industrial Relations Act, 1960.
Whether the respondent should have been directed to be held entitled to back wages from 1992.
petitioner_arguments: The impugned judgment cannot be sustained in view of the fact that the respondent, in law, was not entitled to be classified as a permanent employee under the provisions of Madhya Pradesh Industrial Relations Act, 1960.
In any event the respondent should not have been directed to be held entitled to back wages from 1992.
respondent_arguments: The Special Leave Petition being barred by limitation, the delay in filing the same should not be condoned;
As the certificates issued in favour of the respondent had been examined by three Courts, this Court should not interfere therewith.
court_reasoning: The 1961 Act provides for classification of employees in five categories.

The 1973 Act and the Rules framed thereunder clearly mandate that all posts should be sanctioned by the State Government and all appointments to the said cadre must be made by the State Government alone.
In the absence of any specific directions contained in the Schedule appended to the Standing Orders, the statute and the statutory rules applicable to the employees of the respondent shall prevail.
Regularisation itself does not imply permanency.
holding: The judgment is upheld. The respondent was not entitled to classification as a permanent employee under the provisions of Madhya Pradesh Industrial Relations Act, 1960. He should not have been directed to be held entitled to back wages from 1992.
